solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Traditional food? Best of era cooked

indicators.note: food that is cooked is altered from its raw state, so the letters are prepared into a new order

explanation.surface: A chef praises a dish as the finest of its period, prepared with care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges the nine letters of BEST OF ERA. The question mark flags the dish as only one example of traditional British fare, the Sunday roast.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sunday roast of beef is the classic English dish, so it is an example of traditional fare.

clue.text: Replace poster flanking road — relief for drivers?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit on either side of the road abbreviation, surrounding it
to replace things is to put them back in a different arrangement, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: ST, short for street, stands in for a road

explanation.surface: Someone is told to put a fresh advertising poster up beside a road, offering motorists a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Replace' rearranges the letters of poster, and 'flanking' wraps them round the road abbreviation. The answer is chiefly North American, for what Britons call a lay-by or service area.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside stopping place is where drivers get relief from the wheel; it is the American term for a lay-by.

clue.text: Irregular sailor on choppy Roman lake

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor

indicators.note: choppy water is broken up and disturbed, so the word Roman is jumbled

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A seaman sets out across a rough Italian lake on an odd course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'choppy' scrambles Roman into a woman's name; 'on' is only a link, as the sailor sits on top in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something irregular departs from the norm, which is what the adjective means.

clue.text: Players parade by the sound of it

indicators.note: this phrase says the synonym for parade is heard rather than seen and spelt another way

parts.note: to troop is to march in procession, as in Trooping the Colour

explanation.surface: Actors march past in a procession, or so it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: A company of touring actors or performers is a troupe, a synonym for a group of players.

clue.text: European speciality largely including fine work

indicators.note: the shortened word takes in the abbreviation for fine, holding it within
largely means most of the word, so its final letter is cut off

parts.note: a forte is someone's speciality or strong point
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A European expert's skill is shown in fine craftsmanship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' trims FORTE to FORT; 'including' puts F inside it to make FFORT, after E.
explanation.definitionFit: Effort is exertion or labour, so it is a synonym for work.

clue.text: Accept smashing of teacup

indicators.note: a smashed teacup is in pieces, so the letters of the phrase are broken and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone resigns themselves to a broken teacup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashing' rearranges the eight letters of OF TEACUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To confront and come to terms with something unwelcome is to accept it; the phrase is a verbal idiom.

clue.text: Artist's support and comfort left

parts.note: ease is comfort or freedom from pain

explanation.surface: A painter values a sturdy stand and a comfortable spot to the left.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter rests a canvas on a wooden stand while working, so it is the artist's physical prop.

clue.text: Graceful manner and energy on expert gaining name

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
the on side in cricket is also called the leg side

indicators.note: the word for expert acquires the name abbreviation, taking it into itself

parts.note: an ace is an expert or star performer

explanation.surface: A dancer's poise comes from vigour and a skilled performer making a name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a cricket term: the on side and leg side are the same half of the field. 'gaining' puts N into ACE to make ANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegance is refined grace in bearing or style, so it is a synonym for a graceful manner.

clue.text: Good person on official list for pedestrian activity

parts.note: ST, saint, is the crossword good person
a roll is an official register of names

explanation.surface: A virtuous person appears on the register for walkers.
explanation.definitionFit: A leisurely walk is something a pedestrian does, so this is a playful description of walking.

clue.text: Hobby Greek character dropped in recent times

indicators.note: the Greek letter is let fall from the front of the hobby word, removing it

parts.note: stamp collecting, philately, is a classic hobby
phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek has given up his pastime recently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' tempts a person; it is the letter PHI.
explanation.definitionFit: Lately is an adverb meaning recently, which is what in recent times also means.

clue.text: Show of good wishes among players, end of festival

indicators.note: among says the answer is found within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Teams exchange greetings as a festival closes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' signals letters hidden across playerS END OF Festival, ignoring the comma.
explanation.definitionFit: A farewell gathering wishing someone well on departure is a demonstration of goodwill.

clue.text: Handy protection on the range?

parts.note: handy suggests useful, but it means for the hand; the range is a kitchen cooker, not open country or a shooting range

explanation.surface: A cowboy or shooter wants convenient cover out on the range.
explanation.walkthrough: Range suggests the prairie or a firing range; here it is a cooking stove, and handy means worn on the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A padded mitt protects the hand when taking dishes out of a hot cooker.

clue.text: English politician in trial creating storm

indicators.note: the abbreviations are placed within the word for trial

parts.note: a test is a trial
MP, Member of Parliament, is the usual crossword politician

explanation.surface: An English Member of Parliament on trial causes uproar.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest is a violent storm, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: A fine feature in football?

definitions.meaning: a punishment such as a sum of money imposed for breaking a rule
a kick at goal awarded for an infringement by the opposition

explanation.definitionFit: A fine is a legal punishment, and football awards a spot kick as punishment for a foul.

clue.text: Make fun of sole mogul with spleen sadly

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lone tycoon is mocked in a bad temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges the fifteen letters of SOLE MOGUL and SPLEEN; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom means to tease someone by telling them something untrue, so it is to make fun of them.

clue.text: Rink alas vandalised in island

indicators.note: something vandalised is damaged and wrecked, so the letters are broken up

explanation.surface: Sadly, a skating rink is wrecked on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vandalised' rearranges the eight letters of RINK ALAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The country south of India in the Indian Ocean is an island nation.

clue.text: Service a company curtailed getting heavy loss

parts.note: Mass is a church service

indicators.note: a curtailed word has its tail docked, losing its last letter

parts.note: a crew is a company of workers

explanation.surface: A church service and a firm are cut back after a severe loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' cuts CREW to CRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A massacre is a slaughter of many people, a heavy loss of life; in sport it is also a heavy defeat.

clue.text: Take action in case?

parts.note: taking action sounds like precaution in case something happens, but a case is a lawsuit and action is legal action

explanation.surface: Someone acts as a precaution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in case' reads as a precaution; it means in a legal case.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring a lawsuit is to take legal action in a court case.

clue.text: Inclination reading revised introduction to text

indicators.note: a revised text is altered, so the letters of reading are rearranged
the introduction of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A scholar's inclination is to revise a reading before introducing the text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' rearranges READING to GRADIEN; 'introduction to' gives T from text.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradient is a slope, and an inclination is a slope or angle.

clue.text: Fire is close to firm in Norfolk town

indicators.note: the letters are put within the town name

parts.note: Diss is a small market town in Norfolk, an English county

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A shooting takes place close to a company in a Norfolk town.
explanation.walkthrough: Diss is a market town in Norfolk, a county in eastern England. 'close to' gives the last letter of firm; 'in' puts IS plus that letter after the town's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss an employee is to sack them, which is also called firing.

clue.text: Artist capturing hearts with a flower

indicators.note: the painter's name seizes the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: Salvador Dali, the Spanish surrealist painter
H is the card-suit abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: A painter wins hearts with a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capturing' puts H inside DALI.
explanation.definitionFit: The dahlia is a garden plant grown for its showy blooms, an example of a flower.

clue.text: Critical cut linked with start of economising

parts.note: to sever is to cut

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Austerity critics complain about cuts made in the name of saving money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of' gives E from economising.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe can mean harshly critical, as in severe criticism, or serious, as in a critical condition.

clue.text: Woman varying habit among volunteers

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed in the middle of the volunteers abbreviation

parts.note: TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force

indicators.note: varying means changing, so the letters of habit are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nun changes her habit while working among volunteers.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's part-time volunteer army. 'varying' turns HABIT into ABITH.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabitha is a woman's first name, so this is an example of a woman.

clue.text: The French trapped by fuss in Spanish city

indicators.note: the French article is caught inside the word for fuss

parts.note: a to-do is a fuss or commotion
le is French for the

explanation.surface: French tourists are caught up in a commotion in a Spanish city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trapped by' signals a container: the French article sits inside the word for fuss, a to-do.
explanation.definitionFit: Toledo is a historic city in central Spain, an example of a Spanish city.

clue.text: Lament trouble after rise of work that's spun

indicators.note: the word for trouble comes after the turned word
in a down entry a rising word reads from bottom to top, so it is turned round

parts.note: a spider's web is work that has been spun
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: Someone moans about trouble after spinning work increases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise of' makes the spun work read upwards, as a down entry allows; 'after' puts the trouble behind it. The surface's spinning is a spider's, not a mill's.
explanation.definitionFit: To bewail is to express great sorrow over something, a synonym for lament.

clue.text: Enjoy oneself hugely like organiser of dance?

definitions.meaning: someone holding a formal dance literally possesses a ball

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means having great fun, and read literally it describes someone hosting a formal dance.

clue.text: Mean team endlessly in training to come out

indicators.note: training reshapes someone, so the letters are rearranged
endlessly means without its end, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: taken as written before the cut

explanation.surface: A nasty team trains without end before emerging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts TEAM to TEA; 'in training' rearranges MEAN plus TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to issue or flow out from a source, so it means to come out.

clue.text: District containing new sports venue

indicators.note: the word for district holds the letter for new inside it

parts.note: an area is a district

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood includes a newly built stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is an enclosed space for sporting contests, an example of a sports venue.

clue.text: Soothing time on fell without fellow getting agitated

indicators.note: something agitated is stirred and shaken up, so the letters are rearranged
without says the letter for fellow is removed from the word fell

explanation.surface: A walker finds calm after time on the hills, though a companion grows restless.
explanation.walkthrough: A fell is a hill in northern England. 'without' takes F from FELL, leaving ELL; 'getting agitated' rearranges TIME ON plus ELL.
explanation.definitionFit: An emollient cream softens and soothes the skin; figuratively it means calming.
